# GameController

**Area:** [Games & 3D](../COVERAGE.md#games) · **Apple:** [GameController](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller) · **Issues:** [`area:games`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Agames)

## How isim implements it

- **Passthrough:** host gamepads through SDL3 (`isim/runtime/host_gamepad.c`).
- **Adapted:** `GCVirtualController` is drawn by isim; the keyboard comes from the host.
- **Objective-C:** `#import <GameController/GameController.h>` and `-framework GameController` (`isim/sdk-src/Frameworks/GameController`) reach the Swift overlay's classes under their Objective-C names; `isim/swift/overlays/GameController/ObjC.swift` has the entry points for the Swift-only types (`GCKeyCode`, the player index, haptic localities, `GCDevice`) and `isim/frameworks/GameController/GameController.m` the constants, GCMotion's C structs, and the start of controller discovery when an Objective-C app runs.

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |

| GameController's Objective-C interface: `GCController` (`controllers`, `current`, `controllerWithExtendedGamepad` / `MicroGamepad`, discovery, `playerIndex`, profiles, `battery`, `light`, `haptics`, `motion`), `GCExtendedGamepad`, `GCMicroGamepad`, `GCDirectionalGamepad`, `GCXboxGamepad`, `GCDualShockGamepad`, `GCDualSenseGamepad` / `GCDualSenseAdaptiveTrigger`, `GCPhysicalInputProfile`, the elements (`GCControllerButtonInput`, `GCControllerAxisInput`, `GCControllerDirectionPad`, `GCControllerTouchpad`, `GCDeviceCursor`), `GCKeyboard` / `GCKeyboardInput` and the `GCKeyCode…` values, `GCMouse` / `GCMouseInput`, `GCVirtualController` and its configurations, `GCDeviceHaptics`, `GCDeviceBattery`, `GCDeviceLight` / `GCColor`, `GCMotion`, the `GCDevice` protocol, the notification, input-name, product-category and haptic-locality constants | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: as the Swift classes; Swift-only: the iOS 17 physical-input API (`GCDevicePhysicalInput` and its protocols), `GCEventViewController`, `GCEventInteraction`, the DualSense positional strengths; the classes are not subclassable from Objective-C. Tested (tests/games-objc: a snapshot gamepad, the host keyboard, a tapped GCVirtualController) |
| `GCController` (`controllers()`, `current`, connect / disconnect / current notifications, `playerIndex`) | ✅ | ≤17 | virtual controller and host gamepads |
| `GCExtendedGamepad`, `GCMicroGamepad` (buttons, d-pad, thumbsticks, triggers, value / pressed / touched handlers) | ✅ | ≤17 | tested with the virtual controller |
| Physical game controllers on the host | ✅ | ≤17 | SDL3 gamepads (Xbox / PlayStation / Switch / generic via SDL's mapping database) polled at 60 Hz: each becomes a `GCController` with `GCExtendedGamepad` (+ micro profile), `vendorName` from SDL, `productCategory` from the SDL pad type; `ISIM_GAMEPADS=0` disables. Tested through an SDL virtual joystick (`gamepad` script command), not a physical pad |
| Gamepad rumble: `GCController.haptics`, `GCDeviceHaptics` (`supportedLocalities`, `createEngine(withLocality:)`), `GCHapticsLocality`, `GCHapticDurationInfinite` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a host pad's haptics make CoreHaptics engines whose haptic events drive its two rumble motors through SDL (intensity split over the low- and high-frequency motors by sharpness); the handles only: trigger localities give no engine; snapshots and the virtual controller have none; tested (HelloSpriteKit2, test_spritekit2: the virtual test pad logs the rumble) |
| `GCKeyboard.coalesced`, `GCKeyboardInput` (`button(forKeyCode:)`, `keyChangedHandler`, `isAnyKeyPressed`), `GCKeyCode` | ✅ | ≤17 | the host keyboard; key presses and releases arrive as USB HID usages (scripts: `keydown`/`keyup`) |
| `GCVirtualController` (iOS 15) | 🟡 | ≤17 | thumbsticks, d-pad, A/B/X/Y, shoulders, triggers and menu drawn over the key window; element configurations only hide elements (custom paths ignored) |
| `GCController.battery`, `GCDeviceBattery` (`batteryLevel`, `batteryState`) | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough: SDL's power info of a host pad, read when asked (nil for wired pads and snapshots); the `gamepad battery` script command sets the virtual pad's; tested (HelloSpriteKit2) |
| `GCController.light`, `GCDeviceLight` (`color`), `GCColor` | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough: the colour lights the pad's light bar (DualShock 4 / DualSense; other pads ignore it); tested (HelloSpriteKit2: the virtual pad's LED) |
| `GCController.motion`, `GCMotion` (`sensorsActive`, `sensorsRequireManualActivation`, `acceleration`, `rotationRate`, `gravity` / `userAcceleration` / `attitude` and their setters, `setState(fromMotion:)`, `valueChangedHandler`), `GCAcceleration`, `GCRotationRate`, `GCQuaternion` | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough: a host pad's accelerometer (in g, gravity included) and gyroscope (rad/s), read at 60 Hz while `sensorsActive`; like iOS for DualShock / DualSense, the sensors need manual activation and there is no gravity / user-acceleration split or attitude; the `gamepad motion` script command feeds the virtual pad; tested (HelloSpriteKit2) |
| `GCMouse` (`current`, `mice()`, connect / current notifications), `GCMouseInput` (`mouseMovedHandler`, `leftButton`, `rightButton`, `middleButton`, `auxiliaryButtons`, `scroll`), `GCDeviceCursor` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the host pointer over the device window (relative motion in points with y up, buttons, the scroll wheel), connected once it moves; the pointer still taps the device as touches; `mouse` script commands drive it; tested (HelloSpriteKit2) |
| Product profiles: `GCDualSenseGamepad` (`touchpadButton`, `touchpadPrimary`, `touchpadSecondary`, adaptive `leftTrigger` / `rightTrigger`), `GCDualShockGamepad`, `GCXboxGamepad` (`buttonShare`, `paddleButton1`…`4`), `GCDirectionalGamepad`, `GCControllerTouchpad` (`button`, `touchSurface`, `touchState`, `touchDown` / `touchMoved` / `touchUp`), `GCPhysicalInputProfile.touchpads` / `allTouchpads`, the `GCInput…` names | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough: the profile follows SDL3's pad type (PS5, PS4, Xbox One / 360; others stay `GCExtendedGamepad`); share, paddles and the touchpad are SDL's buttons and first touchpad (two fingers, -1…1, y up); the Xbox paddles exist only on pads SDL reports them for; host pads are never `GCDirectionalGamepad` (a micro gamepad with a d-pad); tested (HelloSpriteKit2: `gamepad connect … as ps5` / `as xbox`, touch, share, paddle) |
| `GCDualSenseAdaptiveTrigger` (`setModeOff()`, feedback / weapon / vibration / slope feedback modes, the positional modes, `mode`, `status`, `armPosition`, `PositionalAmplitudes`, `PositionalResistiveStrengths`, `discretePositionCount`) | 🟡 | ≤17 | passthrough: each mode goes to the pad as a DualSense effect report (SDL's DS5 layout); adapted: the positional modes use the first zone with a value and the strongest one (one zone), slope feedback a constant resistance; `status` is `.unknown` (SDL does not read it back); tested (the virtual pad logs the effect report) |
| `GCController.input`, `GCControllerLiveInput` (`buttons`, `dpads`, `elements`, subscripts by name, `elementValueDidChangeHandler`, `capture()`, `inputStateQueueDepth`, `inputStateAvailableHandler`, `nextInputState()`, `queue`, `unmapped`), `GCControllerInputState`, `GCDevicePhysicalInput`, `GCDevicePhysicalInputState`, `GCDevicePhysicalInputStateDiff`, `GCPhysicalInputElementCollection`, the element protocols (`GCButtonElement`, `GCDirectionPadElement`, `GCAxisElement`, `GCSwitchElement`), the input protocols (`GCLinearInput`, `GCPressedStateInput`, `GCTouchedStateInput`, `GCAxisInput`, `GCAxis2DInput`, `GCRelativeInput`, `GCSwitchPositionInput`), `GCPhysicalInputSource`, the element names (`GCButtonElementName`, `GCDirectionPadElementName`, `GCAxisElementName`, `GCSwitchElementName`, `GCPhysicalInputElementName`) | ✅ | 17.0 | adapted: the elements wrap the controller's profile elements (the same values and timing); every element change queues a state with the elements that changed since the previous one; host pads have no axis or switch elements (`axes` and `switches` are empty); `sources` are empty; latencies are 0; `unmapped` is the same input (isim does not remap); tested (HelloSpriteKit2: named elements, handlers, the state queue, `capture()`) |
